ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\cos A=\frac{1}{3}$, then what is the value of $\sin B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle C=90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle A+\angle B=90^\circ$,\\
hence $\sin B=\cos A=\boxed{\frac{1}{3}}$.

Segment BC is horizontal, segment AC is vertical, and there is a right-angle marker at C, so AC is perpendicular to BC and AB is the hypotenuse. Reasoning: Since angle C is 90°, angles A and B are complementary, so A + B = 90°. Therefore B = 90° - A. Using the cofunction identity, sin B = sin(90° - A) = cos A. Given cos A = 1/3, it follows that sin B = 1/3.
